subject: Taxes
title: The Laffer Curve
description: A fast breakdown of The Laffer Curve for builders.

hook.text: Arthur Laffer drew a curve on a napkin in 1974. He argued raising tax rates past a certain point cuts total revenue.

buildup.text: The logic: at 0% tax, revenue is zero. At 100% tax, nobody works, so revenue is also zero.

discovery.text: Ronald Reagan used the Laffer Curve to justify massive tax cuts in 1981, arguing lower rates would increase revenue.

twist.text: Deficits tripled under Reagan. Critics say the curve was used to justify cuts that never paid for themselves.

climax.text: The Laffer Curve is real in theory but hard to locate in practice. Nobody agrees where the optimal rate is.

punchline.text: One napkin, one curve. Still debated 50 years later.

quiz.question: What does the Laffer Curve claim?
options: Higher rates always mean more revenue
Past a certain point, higher rates reduce revenue
